description: On July 14, 1789, Parisians stormed a fortress which contained only **7 prisoners**. This gesture became the symbol of the French Revolution.

hero.hook: On July 14, 1789, Paris stormed a fortress… for gunpowder.

blocks.text: On **July 14, 1789**, a crowd of Parisians marched on the **Bastille**, an old fortress east of Paris. They are not coming to free thousands of prisoners. They especially want **powder** to defend themselves.
That day, King **Louis XVI** saw his capital slip away from him. A riot for weapons becomes the founding act of the **French Revolution**. Here's how.

In 1789, the kingdom was ruined. Helping the American colonies during [[American War of Independence]] was very expensive. To raise new taxes, Louis XVI convened the **States General** in May: an assembly of the clergy, the nobility and the rest of the people.

blocks.caption: The States General of 1789: the Third Estate facing the clergy and the nobility.

blocks.text: Under the [[Ancien Régime and the three orders]], the company is divided into three. Clergy and nobility retain their privileges. The **Third Estate**, almost everyone, has only one vote. Blocked, he proclaimed himself **National Assembly** on **June 17**. Three days later, at the **Oath of the Jeu de Paume**, the deputies swear not to separate before having written a constitution.
The king seemed to give in, but he placed about **30,000 soldiers** around Paris. On **July 11**, he dismissed **Jacques Necker**, his very popular Minister of Finance. Panic spreads to the capital.

sections.title: France on the verge of bankruptcy

blocks.text: The **12** and **July 13**, Paris is rebelling. The grant barriers (taxes at the entrance to the city) are burned. We pillage the armories. On the morning of **14**, the crowd seized approximately **32,000 rifles** from the **Invalids**. The powder is missing.

blocks.caption: The storming of the Bastille, July 14, 1789.

blocks.text: That day, the Bastille contained only **7 prisoners**: 4 forgers, 2 men deemed insane and an aristocrat. Its strength was above all in what it represented.

Rumor has it that the gunpowder is in the Bastille. For many, this prison embodies the king's arbitrariness, especially because of the [[The lettre de cachet]], an order of confinement without trial. Governor **from Launay** refuses to open. Around **1:30 p.m.**, shots rang out: **98 dead** among the attackers. Soldiers passing by the people bring cannons. At the end of the afternoon, the fortress fell. De Launay is lynched in the street.

On **July 15**, Louis XVI is awakened. “Is this a revolt? » he asks. They replied: “No Sire, it’s a revolution. » Irony of the calendar: in his hunting journal, the king had noted “Nothing” on the 14th.

The entrepreneur **Palloy**, responsible for demolishing the Bastille, had dominoes cut from its stones and offered a set of them to the king's son, "so that he could play with the remains of despotism".

The king recalls Necker, withdraws his troops and accepts the **tricolor cockade**. In the countryside, the news fueled [[The Great Fear]]: the peasants, fearing revenge from the nobles, burned the papers of seigniorial rights. On the night of **August 4, 1789**, the Assembly abolished the privileges.
The next day, the Bastille was demolished. A year later, the **Federation Day** celebrates unity. But July 14 did not become a national holiday until **1880**, under the Third Republic.

blocks.text: **July 14, 1789**, Paris takes the Bastille for gunpowder. This gesture transforms a financial crisis into a revolution and precipitates the end of the order of privileges.
